speaker: Penny
text: Do you mind if I stay here tonight? The couch is good.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Or my bed. I just got new pillows. My daughter, Janet. Hold that thought, Leonard, a moment.

speaker: Leonard
text: No, yeah, take the couch. Let me guess, you have a problem with this. It's up to you, crazy person's choice.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Where do I begin?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Well, first, we don't have house guests. Frankly, if I could afford the rent, I'd ask you to leave.

speaker: Leonard
text: Your friendship means a lot to me as well. What else?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Well, our earthquake supplies. We have a two-man, two-day kit. So, if there is an earthquake and the three of us are trapped here, we could be out of food by tomorrow afternoon.

speaker: Leonard
text: So?

speaker: Leonard
text: I'm sorry, are you suggesting that if we let Penny stay, we might succumb to cannibalism?

speaker: Sheldon
text: No one ever thinks it'll happen until it does.

speaker: Leonard
text: Penny, if you promise not to chew the flesh off our bones while we sleep, you can stay.

speaker: Penny
text: What?

speaker: Sheldon
text: He's engaging in reductio ad absurdum. It's the logical fallacy of extending someone's argument to ridiculous proportions and then criticizing the result, and I do not appreciate it.

speaker: Leonard
text: I'll get you a blanket and a pillow.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Okay, well, since I'm obviously being ignored here, let's go over the morning schedule. I use the bathroom from 7 to 7:20. Plan your ablutions and bodily functions accordingly.

speaker: Penny
text: How am I supposed to plan my bodily functions?

speaker: Sheldon
text: I suggest no liquids after 11 p.m.

speaker: Leonard
text: There you go.

speaker: Penny
text: Thanks, Leonard.

speaker: Leonard
text: Thank you, bro.
